chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Bajali, the cousin of Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Saif ibn Amirah, from Abu al-Subah Nuhaym al-Ta'izi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever recites the Tasbih of al-Zahra (peace be upon her) and then seeks forgiveness, his sins will be forgiven. It is one hundred [times] by tongue, and one thousand in the Scale. It drives away Satan and pleases the Merciful.'

key_terms.الْمِیزَانِ: The Scale (of deeds on the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.تَسْبِیحَ الزَّهْرَاءِ: Tasbih of al-Zahra (a specific devotional formula attributed to Fatima al-Zahra)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward and significance of reciting Tasbih of Fatima al-Zahra?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (a.s.) narrates that reciting the specific supplication known as 'Tasbih of al-Zahra' followed by seeking forgiveness guarantees forgiveness. This practice, consisting of one hundred recitations, carries the weight of one thousand in the Hereafter's scale, repels Satan, and pleases God. In Shia tradition, this dhikr is uniquely attributed to Fatima al-Zahra (s.a.) and is often recited after the Fajr prayer, serving as a spiritual shield against Satan and a means of attaining divine pleasure through the intercession of the Prophet's daughter.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2.  Imam  Muhammad  Baqir  (a.s.)  said,  “One  who  seeks forgiveness  after  reciting  Tasbih  of  Zahra  (s.a.)  will  be forgiven. Although it is recited a hundred times, it is equal to one  thousand  Tasbih  in  Mizan.  It  keeps  Satan  away  and pleases the Merciful.”
